answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can run bonded beacons: each new identity posts a refundable stake before its beacon is co-signed by established agents, who admit it only after varied, sustained activity. A comet burst of hundreds of wallets from one operator gains nothing - every clone locks the same collateral through the same maturity window, so capital sits idle unproductively. Peers also flag umber clusters of identical timing and slash stakes when clones vote in lockstep. Attacker cost grows linearly per fake agent while influence stays capped, so mass identity farming never pays.
